missionPremise: The preamble's rule 3 says a missing cityKey refuses. Eight request-scoped routes and four module-level defaults in smartcity-dashboards did the opposite: a caller who named no city was handed the DEMO pack's identity, shell state, domains, pipeline and compose under a 200, reading exactly like a real city's records - and the client's own boot default made a BARE VISIT land on that same demo. The premise held, in both halves, and was measured rather than inherited: G-159 enumerated the seven remaining routes in its close, and CP1 re-measured the list at current main by symbol AND by literal before any edit.
completionPredicate: Every route that reads a city pack refuses a request that names no city and still answers a request that names one; the demo's public URL names it explicitly and a bare visit states that it has none; the change is proven by violation in the test runner AND on the deployed surface in both directions. ALL ARE MET AND MEASURED. 7 of 7 probeable routes refuse keyless, empty and whitespace cityKey with 400 city_key_required on the deployed app and 0 serve a resolved demo pack; the same three cells were 200-with-demo on the same URL before the deploy; a named pack is still 200, an unknown pack still 404 and a tenant-private pack still 401, so an ABSENCE was refused rather than the route; and the bare visit now renders the stated no-city panel with the demo pack's name nowhere in the document. The one cell this lane does NOT measure live is the municode POST's own 400, which its caller-authorisation gate answers first for an anonymous caller; it is proven in src/city-refusal.test.mjs with that gate open, and that bound is stated on the artifact rather than hidden behind a passing status code.

probe.artifactIsThePostFixLeg: The skeleton names `probe.artifact` as a single path under _inbox/, and this is it: the artifact produced AFTER this lane's merge was deployed, carrying the four cells for all eight routes and the client reading. The PRE-fix leg is cited beside it as probe.preFixArtifact, because the dispatch asks for a PAIRED control and this lane has both halves; the post-fix leg is the one the closure claim rests on, and the pre-fix leg is the one that shows the defect was on the surface.

It is not, and stating that plainly is the point. scripts/surface-probe.mjs in doc_repo is the PROPERTY surface instrument: it probes parcels (48021:34049, 48453:113408, ...) against facets, situs, gis ring, near-bbox and cortex, and it was written FOR the OPS-23 property rows the enforcement gate gates. It has no predicate for an HTTP route on d12-main-uat and cannot have one; it was run during this lane and confirms its own scope by probing ten parcels and reporting NOT MEASURED per parcel leg. G-161 is a smartcity-dashboards row, and the gate that reads probe.artifact applies to rows P-151..P-167, P-169..P-174, P-186, P-195, P-198 and P-200 - G-161 is not among them. contradicted: THREE. (1) The dispatch enumerates seven server routes plus the client. LESSON: When a client stops defaulting a required parameter, grep the INSTRUMENTS that were pointed at the defaulted value. This lane's a11y gate had 24 targets built on the client resolving a pack for a URL that named none; deleting the default would have pointed the whole gate at the no-city panel and turned it red on every title, and nobody would have connected the red to the server change. The instrument is part of the blast radius.

A substring test cannot tell a symbol from a sentence about it. This lane's own probe reported the post-fix app.js as still importing DEFAULT_CITY_KEY, because the file explains in comments why the default was deleted. Strip comments before asserting on CODE, and name the field for what it actually reads - otherwise the instrument answers a question about prose.

Read the hash back AND compare it to the merge commit. d12-main-uat has no deploy-on-push, so merging deploys nothing and the previous deployment keeps serving; a lane that read source_commit_hash right after the PR merged would have read the PREVIOUS commit and filed it as proof.

A hash equality is true only at a MOMENT, and a shared UAT app moves under you. This lane recorded 'origin/main = da3d611' during its probe, then the concurrent lane merged PR #74 and origin/main became 7487d7c while this lane was still writing its close; worse, that same lane shares d12-main-uat and COULD have redeployed it, which would have left this lane's proof describing a surface that no longer existed. The fix is two cheap acts, and both were done: re-read the deployment status at close time rather than trusting the read taken minutes earlier, and write each hash equality with the moment it was measured. A close that states a tip equality in the present tense is a claim that decays silently between the probe and the reader.

Refuse an ABSENCE, never the route. Every route in this lane still answers a named pack (200), an unknown pack (404) and a tenant-private pack anonymously (401); only the unnamed cell changed. That is what keeps a correctness fix from being an outage, and it is cheap to assert in the same harness.

One helper stated once, with the reason REQUIRED at each call site, is how eight copies of the same guard stop drifting - and the reason is what makes the next route's author say what their own 400 is protecting instead of inheriting a sentence that does not fit.
DEAD_END: Do not make the municode POST's 400 visible to an anonymous probe by reordering its caller-authorisation gate. Its gate answers first by design; the refusal is proven in the test runner with the gate open, and reordering production authorisation to make a probe read better is measuring the instrument with the product.
Do not keep a silent city default to protect a demo URL. The demo's bare URL was the ONLY thing depending on the default, and the operator's ruling was to make the demo explicit instead.

Do not read the a11y gate's scanned-surface list as being about the packs it scans: SCANNED_PACKS is [empty-city] and the default pack is NOT in it, so a lookup restricted to the scanned list silently drops the default pack's name out of every expected title.
